title: World No. 47 Rakshitha Ramraj Stuns Her Idol Chen Yufei at Hong Kong Open
excerpt: The 19-year-old from Coimbatore beat the former Olympic champion 21-18, 24-22 to reach her maiden Super 500 quarter-final, a day after her first top-20 win.
body:
• Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj, 19, beat world No. 4 and former Olympic champion Chen Yu Fei 21-18, 24-22 in the second round of the LI-NING Hong Kong Open on Thursday.
  • It is the world No. 47's first win over a top-10 player and takes her into her maiden Super 500 quarter-final.
  • The win came a day after she upset Denmark's Mia Blichfeldt, her first victory over a top-20 player.
  • She next faces Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong for a place in the semi-finals.

Nineteen-year-old Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj produced the result of her career at the Hong Kong Open on Thursday, beating former Olympic champion Chen Yu Fei 21-18, 24-22 in straight games to reach her maiden Super 500 quarter-final. The Indian, ranked 47th in the world, toppled the pre-tournament favourite and world No. 4 in the second round, according to the Badminton World Federation.

The Coimbatore shuttler, who trains at the Pullela Gopichand Academy in Hyderabad, used overhead deceptions to keep Chen guessing and attacked to take control of the rallies, closing out a tight second game 24-22, India Today reported. The BWF said she became the first player ranked outside the top 30 to beat Chen since Indonesia's Gregoria Mariska Tunjung in 2017.

"She's my biggest idol and I still can't believe I won against her. This will be one of the most memorable days in my badminton career."

— Rakshitha Ramraj, speaking after the match

"I was just playing free, I was playing all my strokes and they were going good," she said, adding that she had been preparing for a third game before closing the match out in two. "I'm very thankful to all my coaches for supporting me throughout this journey."

A breakthrough built over two seasons

The Chen win was Rakshitha's second upset in 24 hours. In the opening round she beat Denmark's Mia Blichfeldt, her first victory over a top-20 player, before recording her first top-10 scalp a day later. The BWF reported that her family moved from Coimbatore to Hyderabad six years ago so she could train at the Gopichand academy, a decision that required her father to quit his job with the railways.

Her rise has been gathering pace since 2024, when she won the Slovenia Open and the India International Challenge. She added the Sri Lanka International title in February this year, won the Hanoi International in June, and followed it with the India International title, where she beat Scotland's Kirsty Gilmour, then ranked 25th in the world, in the final, according to India Today.

What comes next

Rakshitha now faces Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong in the quarter-finals, her first meeting with the Thai player, with a semi-final place at a Super 500 event at stake. Whatever the outcome, the Hong Kong run is already the biggest result of her career — and the first time she has beaten a player ranked inside the world's top 10.
